messages:
Maria: did a targeted perf run switching attention + ffw to FP8 per-channel calib. seeing tail latency creep on long seqs, weird batching behavior.

Maria: profiler excerpt (model=redwood-gpt-12B, batch_target=8, seq=3072):
```
kernel_selector.cc snapshot:
  fp8/per-channel  hot_path: 54ms
  fp8/per-tensor  hot_path: 40ms
  int8/kernel      hot_path: 42ms
batching/metrics:
  active_window_ms: 7
  fallback_smallbatches: 23
  shard_fallback_syncs: 4
kv/cache:
  warmup_misses: 18%
  kv/lock_wait: 16ms
overall/token_latency: 0.78 -> 0.95 (+22%)
```

AJ: hmm. did kernel selection thresholds change? or is this purely from the new calib stats?

Maria: only swapped calib mode + new scale table. same runtime heuristics.

Kai: per-channel tends to make some channels have very tiny scales or huge ones depending on outliers. that can increase dynamic range when dequantized -> more variance in KV values -> cache pattern shift.

Sasha: can you dump the scale distribution? we might be hitting denorms or int overflow on certain kernels.

Maria: sample scales (attention qkv layer 4): [0.09, 0.085, 0.072, 0.0004, 0.1, 0.11, 0.08]

Ben: that 0.0004 stands out. per-channel amplifies its quantized integers after inverse scale. leads to spikes in activation magnitudes.

Maya: operationally, when many shards see those spikes around the same tokens, batching windows shrink (we hit min-latency thresholds) and runtime falls back to smaller batches simultaneously -> synchronized small-batch fallback across shards -> throughput hit.

Maria: confirmed: trace shows 4 shards hit `batching/fallback_smallbatches` at the same token indices.

AJ: mitigation ideas:
- percentile clipping during calib (e.g., 99.5th/0.1th)
- min_scale threshold for per-channel, below which we switch to per-tensor or clamp
- introduce small random jitter into batching window close to boundary to de-sync shard fallback

Kai: also consider hybrid quant layout: per-tensor on KV matmuls (most sensitive for cache) + per-channel on FFN.

Sasha: agree. propose a guarded calibration run with automated perf check. steps:
1) calibrate with clip_low=0.005, clip_high=99.9p
2) produce scale table and run quick perf sweep (smoke) across seq buckets
3) if median token_lat increases >5% or tail >10% reject calib

Maria: i'll run command:
```
./bin/calibrate --model=redwood-gpt-12B --mode=per-channel --clip-low=0.005 --percentile=99.9 --out=scales/pch-guarded.json
./bin/perf_sweep --scales=scales/pch-guarded.json --buckets=256,1024,3072 --runs=3
```

Ben: in parallel i'll patch runtime to: add `min_batch=2` enforcement for fp8_per_channel kernels and a 3-8ms random jitter to `batching/window` if we're within 10% of the boundary.

Maya: and i'll update sampler: stratified by source, cap max per-source examples, ensure we include tail long-seq examples, and run outlier trimming (global and per-channel percentile).

AJ: CI gate: `quantization_ci` should run a lightweight perf sweep in PR and fail if token_ms regression >5% or kv/lock_wait increases by >5ms.

Kai: small auto-fallback: if any layer has scale < 0.001 or NaN, runtime will mark that layer "unstable" and prefer per-tensor path for that op. I'll draft a small patch.

Maria: quick repro note: swapping back to old per-tensor scales returns perf to baseline, so it's definitely calibration-driven.

Sasha: logging action items:
- Maria: guarded calib + perf sweep + post results (today)
- Maya: sampler stratification and outlier trimming (WIP)
- Ben: batching jitter + min_batch enforcement patch (WIP)
- Kai: auto-fallback tiny-scale detection (PR)
- AJ: quant CI perf gate (PR)

infra-bot: deploy-checker: no active deploys in runtime cluster during profiling window.

Maria: please also add `kv/lock_wait`, `kv/warmup_miss_rate`, and `batching/fallback_smallbatches` to the perf dashboard for quant experiments.

Ben: will add metrics + a small alert if `fallback_smallbatches` spikes >10 in a 1m window.

Maria: thanks everyone — running the guarded pass now. will post logs & the scale dump when done. :rocket:
